channel.title: Inbox Signal — Week of 9–16 Nov 2026
channel.description: Weekly digest of linked items from the newsletter inbox, 9–16 November 2026.

item.title: Code review has become a stage: the job is now to classify, route and rebalance review
item.description: In LinearB’s benchmark of 8.1M PRs, AI-generated PRs merge at 32.7% against 84.4% for human PRs, and agentic PRs wait 5.3 times longer for a reviewer.

item.title: incident.io cut AI spend per developer from $4,500 to $1,600 a month while shipping more PRs
item.description: Spend runs near $1.6M for the year, peaking above $300K in July, roughly 80% Claude and 20% Cursor.

item.title: Buy hosted agents; build only the rules file and the gates
item.description: The newsletter cites Bloomberg on Uber, where more than 70% of PRs come from agents and review time rose from about 3 hours in 2024 to about 9 hours in 2026.

item.title: LinkedIn’s AI reviewer runs parallel subagents across 40,000+ PRs a week
item.description: The final design uses independent parallel subagents, a merge step, a verification step, and layered rules for company, repo and PR.

item.title: A three-month rewrite took nine months, and Brooks’s Law explains why
item.description: Milanović describes a rewrite that hit 140 special cases, added five engineers and ten agents, built 40 microservices, and broke the biggest customer’s import in month nine.

item.title: Nvidia’s board pushed Jensen Huang out within days, despite his founder control
item.description: The board opened a probe on 8 November, and Huang resigned as CEO and director on 12 November.

item.title: Anthropic opens its IPO roadshow with a $70–$78 price range, pricing on 18 November
item.description: The post gives the range, pricing on 18 November and a Nasdaq listing as ANT on 19 November.

item.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen targets fast, cheap agent work at $1.50 in and $7.50 out per million tokens
item.description: TLDR AI reports a score of 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ahead of Gemini 4 Argon.

item.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 launch with up to 30% faster output
item.description: Both models share one architecture, with gains in coding, reasoning and vision.

item.title: OpenAI reportedly raises $11B at a $1.25T valuation, short of its earlier target
item.description: TechCrunch reports the round could reach $20B before it closes, and that it falls short of the $30B the company had sought, amid valuation uncertainty.

item.title: Horizon3’s AI hacker took 14 minutes 25 seconds to own a patched, Defender-protected lab
item.description: NodeZero compromised the GOAD lab, with Defender on every host, with no humans involved.

item.title: Gartner: AI creates 10.6M jobs and eliminates 8.9M by 2030
item.description: The forecast excludes China and India.

item.title: Ramp: AI token spending grew only 1.5% across August and September
item.description: Ramp’s transaction data shows AI token spend flat through the two months despite rising usage, then growing again in October.

item.title: OpenAI’s GPT-6 Cyber produced 948 Linux kernel findings, and the two sources disagree on what they are
item.description: The Batch counts 2,308 candidates, 1,724 confirmed, 1,169 exploits and 948 patches, at about $1,280 per finding.

item.title: Runway’s Praxis-1 is an open-weight 27B robotics model under Apache 2.0
item.description: Runway reports 46.2% success on NVIDIA’s RoboLab-120 benchmark across 1,200 episodes, and says the model supports full and LoRA fine-tuning on NVIDIA hardware.

item.title: Most decisions are two-way doors, and treating them as one-way kills velocity
item.description: Stanier cites Bezos’s Type 1 and Type 2 framing and warns about one-way doors disguised as two-way ones, such as public APIs, data models and customer commitments.

item.title: Architects become the bottleneck when teams learn that asking the architect is the safe route
item.description: Each request seems reasonable, but together they form an unofficial architecture gate.

item.title: Correctness comes from types and realistic workloads, not from more unit tests
item.description: Sean Allen of Antithesis argues that sum types with exhaustive matching turn a forgotten case into a compile error.

item.title: Managed personal agents hand too much power to firms that may not be trustworthy
item.description: Grok Bot launched at $300 a month, then dropped to $30, and its quotas were halved.

item.title: About one in four two-founder teams lost a co-founder within four years
item.description: Carta tracked 13,133 founders from US two-founder teams (2015–2024), and puts the 2017 cohort’s departure rate at 24.1%.

item.title: Two $15K hires turn a default-alive startup into a default-dead one by month 16
item.description: The example company has $2M cash, $170K monthly expenses and $40K monthly revenue growing 7% a month, giving 15.4 months of runway.

item.title: People read the same leadership statement as either an audit or an aspiration
item.description: Some people compare what leaders say with actual incentives and feel uncomfortable.

item.title: The gap between elite and median teams keeps widening: 8x, then 9x, then 10x
item.description: Quarterly research shows elite teams’ throughput advantage grew from 8x in Q1 to 9x in Q2 and 10x in Q3.

item.title: Resend moved its email API from Node to Go in seven weeks
item.description: At a 50% rollout, median latency fell from 58 ms to 31 ms and memory per task from about 1.3 GB to 180 MB.

item.title: Cloudflare’s targeted DNS zone builds cut peak memory from 79 GiB to 12 GiB
item.description: The same change took the median build from 7.7 seconds to 3.3 seconds.

item.title: Apache HTTP Server has a remote-code-execution race; upgrade to 2.4.71 or disable HTTP/2
item.description: The flaw is a race in assign_headers() in the HTTP/2 module.

item.title: GitHub used Copilot agents to port the Copilot runtime from TypeScript to Rust
item.description: The body says 430K lines of TypeScript moved, at about $120K of AI tokens (136B tokens); the intro says nearly 800K lines.

item.title: An independent threat model found 30 Linkerd threats, and only one was a software bug
item.description: 28 of the 30 threats are rated medium or high, and most come from default and configuration choices.

item.title: X rebuilt its web app as one server, in under six months
item.description: One Fastify and React app with streaming SSR replaces three servers.

item.title: Google’s Gemini Decisions API evaluates up to 1,000 yes/no or rubric questions in one pass
item.description: The newsletter gives the price as $0.10 per two million input tokens, with outputs free.

item.title: Dropbox’s scoped agent tasks delivered 22 accessibility fixes and cleared 53 test cleanups in a week
item.description: Engineers reviewed the agent output.

item.title: NVIDIA’s NeMo case: malformed agent tool calls fell from 142 to zero at Dassault
item.description: The evaluation score rose 28% and each run made 35% fewer tool calls, according to NVIDIA’s case study.

item.title: No model escaped the VM-host boundary in Perplexity’s SPACE tests, but several bypassed network controls
item.description: Twelve models were tested against an agent sandbox.

item.title: Agent debugging needs OpenTelemetry traces, and the key metric is cost per successful task
item.description: The guest post treats the whole agent harness (reasoning loop, memory, evals, guardrails and human-in-the-loop) as the unit to trace.

item.title: Agents opened more than 40% of GitHub PRs in September, up from 17% in March
item.description: The figure comes from GitHub’s Octoverse, as relayed by ByteByteGo, which says more than 40% of September PRs started with agents.

item.title: Partial failure: losing 2 of 10 cache nodes can double database load and cascade
item.description: The preview covers partial failure, split-brain and cascading failure, with defences such as idempotency keys, the outbox pattern, sagas, quorums, fencing tokens and circuit breakers.

item.title: Idempotency keys alone don’t give exactly-once payments
item.description: The post treats exactly-once as a semantic achieved with three patterns: idempotency keys, deduplication and a transactional outbox.

item.title: Deploying is not releasing: blast radius, detection and rollback decide the pattern
item.description: The post frames the choice around three questions.

item.title: Continuous batching and PagedAttention are the main levers for LLM inference cost
item.description: Iteration-level scheduling, from Orca and vLLM, lets batches refill as requests finish.

item.title: Shield AI is buying Echodyne for $5.3B, with $500M tied to targets
item.description: $4.8B is paid upfront and $500M depends on milestones.

item.title: Horizon3 went from $1M ARR in September 2021 to over $100M in October 2026
item.description: Its figures show 95% gross and 125% net retention, with about 80% of the first 3,000 customers coming through MSSPs.

item.title: Of 222 funded pitch decks, 121 belong to pre-seed or seed companies
item.description: Those companies raised $117B in total.

item.title: The one-line VC method overprices a $4M seed by 2.9 times
item.description: The naive method gives $38.6M pre-money, but once later rounds dilute the stake the same investment is worth $13.2M.

item.title: A data room has 71 documents in three tiers, with 43 needed for confirmatory diligence
item.description: The tiers are 4 first-look, 24 partner diligence and 43 confirmatory documents.

item.title: LinkedIn comment outreach booked 321 calls in two months, according to the vendor
item.description: Prospects who had commented on a target’s post replied 34.2% of the time, against 9.9% for company-page followers, in a two-week test of 2,253 prospects.

item.title: The EU’s Digital Fairness Act proposal would ban dark patterns and hard-to-cancel subscriptions
item.description: The proposal allows fines up to 6% of global revenue, and gives the Commission direct enforcement powers.

item.title: Paired CSS system colours can fail contrast: HighlightText on Highlight reaches 1.98:1
item.description: In Chrome on Android dark mode, that pair reaches only 1.98:1 contrast.

item.title: In a 20-person trial, AI moderators drew less depth than human moderators
item.description: Human moderators averaged 6.9 of 8 themes and the AI moderator 5.0.

item.title: Touch beat trackpad on laptops in one small test, 1.39 s against 1.74 s
item.description: Touch averaged 1.39 seconds against 1.74 for the trackpad across six tasks.

item.title: Accessible LLM chat: announce the finished answer once, not every streamed token
item.description: The guidance is a single live region after streaming, skip links and Control+F6 for moving between regions.

item.title: GitHub’s pull-request overview redesign puts merge readiness at the top
item.description: The redesign is opt-in as a public preview from 5 November.

item.title: Conversational AI swaps feel like redesigns, and users’ expectations move with them
item.description: Nielsen’s 39-minute essay sets out seven principles and 37 guidelines.

item.title: Copy the shape of outliers, not their details
item.description: Huynh’s argument is that outperformers reveal what works, so copy the structure and fill in your own examples rather than the scripts.

item.title: Microsoft 365 outage on 12 November
item.description: Email and Intune were disrupted across Microsoft 365, and Microsoft was still working on the fix at the time of writing, per The Register.

item.title: Yandex restores 97% of customer data
item.description: About 97% of affected data came back after October drone strikes on three data centres.

item.title: Anthropic adds up to $4.3B of Microsoft cloud compute
item.description: Expanded agreements ahead of its planned IPO, per TLDR IT and Data Center Dynamics.

item.title: Google announces a $17B Cheyenne data-centre campus
item.description: It takes over a Crusoe-developed campus, using gas fuel cells, carbon capture and air cooling.

item.title: Adobe opens Creative Cloud to third-party AI assistants
item.description: ChatGPT and Claude would edit Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and After Effects through MCP.

item.title: Gemini in Gmail reaches more Workspace users
item.description: Thread summaries and Help me write roll out on by default for all Workspace users aged 18 and over, starting 10 November.

item.title: Outlook rejects some legitimate email
item.description: SPF and DMARC enforcement is bouncing real messages, per The Register.

item.title: Fly.io patched its fleet over 10 hours
item.description: A Linux kernel flaw let guest VMs read host memory.

item.title: Rust 1.100.0 is stable
item.description: It stabilises the never type and Allocator and DropGuard APIs, and Cargo adds unused-dependency reporting.

item.title: Chrome’s Modern Web Guidance 1.0
item.description: Skills that embed web-platform expertise and browser compatibility data into coding agents.
